name: W Hopf rule
summary: Splitting with a W-node, applying Z(π) to one branch and merging again disconnects the wire.
description:
The W-node (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg. A W-node with no outputs is the state $|0\rangle$ (read as an effect, it is $\langle 0|$), which is the unit of the W-node read as a 'merge'.

The W-node is a Hopf algebra whose antipode is the Pauli Z: splitting a wire with a W-node, applying $Z$ to one of the two branches and merging them again gives $|0\rangle\langle0|$, since the two ways of routing an excitation cancel. This is axiom 5d of Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus.

It is the case $n = m = 1$ of the [W loop rule](../w-loop/), which counts the branches with signs.
